# OWLLM Browser Control (B + C)

## Idea
Give OWLLM the ability to **drive a real browser** — navigate, fill forms, click buttons, do anything a human can — with the user's **own logins intact**. Cloud agents (ChatGPT Operator, etc.) run in *their* sandbox, so your authenticated sessions and 2FA never come along, and login-walled sites block them. OWLLM is **local**, so it can hold a real, persistent, logged-in browser session on the user's own machine.

- **B — dedicated browser.** OWLLM launches its *own* headful Chromium (not your daily Chrome) with a **persistent profile dir**. Log into each site **once** (incl. 2FA); the session survives across runs. Stable — doesn't fight your everyday browser's security.
- **C — the model understands and acts.** The model reads the page and decides the next action turn-by-turn → handles **novel tasks on unseen sites** (the Japanese-signup case). Successful runs saved as **replayable flows**.

## ICP
An OWLLM power-user doing **repetitive or friction-heavy web tasks that require being logged in** — overseas signups, checking multiple portals, form-filling on sites that block cloud agents.

## Architecture (verified against the repo)
1. **`owllm-desktop/resources/tools/browser_daemon.py`** — persistent Playwright Chromium sidecar. Headful + persistent profile (**B**). One-line JSON: `navigate / snapshot / click / fill / press / select / screenshot / get_text / wait / back / reload / tabs / close`. `snapshot` returns the a11y tree, **stamping each interactive element with an index** the model acts on by number.
2. **`owllm-desktop/src-tauri/src/browser.rs`** — `BrowserSession` global (mirrors `mcp.rs`'s `Lazy<TokioMutex<…>>`) keeping the daemon **alive across tool calls**. Commands: `browser_start / browser_cmd / browser_stop / browser_status / browser_ensure` (bootstraps `pip install playwright` + `playwright install chromium` first-run).
3. **`owllm-desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`** — `mod browser;` + register the 5 commands.
4. **`owllm-desktop/ui/src/pages/agentic/localTools.ts`** — `browser_*` tool specs + `executeToolCall` cases (**C-agentic**), plus `browser_save_flow` / `browser_run_flow` for deterministic **record/replay (C)**. Slots into the native GGUF loop (`dispatch.ts`); **no XML path**.

*(No browser engine ships today — the `screenshot_url.py`→`core.twinforge` gap; "Playwright" mentions are test comments. B+C = adding the engine.)*

## Feature Priority
| Feature | Priority |
|---|---|
| Headful Chromium, persistent profile (login once, 2FA survives) | **v1** |
| `navigate/click/fill/press/select` core actions | **v1** |
| `snapshot` = a11y tree with indexed elements | **v1** |
| `screenshot` + `get_text` for page-understanding | **v1** |
| Daemon alive across tool calls (state persists) | **v1** |
| First-run auto-bootstrap (Playwright + Chromium) | **v1** |
| Agentic turn-by-turn drive on unseen sites | **v1** |
| Save run → replayable flow JSON | **v2** |
| Deterministic `browser_run_flow` replay | **v2** |
| Multi-tab orchestration | **v2** |
| Anti-bot resilience + captcha handoff | **v2** |
| Drive user's *live* everyday Chrome (mode A) | **drop** — fights Chrome security, not the wedge |

## GUI Direction
Reuse the **agentic team** surface; the headful Chromium window is the canvas the user watches — no new page for v1. v2: a small **flow library** panel.

## Positioning
Single sharpest wedge: **a local, persistent, logged-in browser session the model can drive.** Cloud agents structurally can't hold the user's real auth; OWLLM can. Auth persistence is the moat; agentic nav + replay are table-stakes automation.

## v1 Scope (locked)
Dedicated headful Chromium + persistent profile (**B**) · core verbs + indexed `snapshot` + `screenshot`/`get_text` · daemon held alive by Rust across the loop · first-run auto-bootstrap · model drives turn-by-turn on unseen sites (**C-agentic**).

## v2 Backlog
Record→replay flows · multi-tab · anti-bot + captcha handoff · flow library UI + scheduling.

## Risks
- **#1 — small local GGUFs are weak at agentic browsing.** Mitigation: allow a cloud driver model when configured; lean on flows/replay so repeats don't need live reasoning.
- **Anti-bot / captcha.** Signup flows often gate on captcha — may need a **human handoff**, not hands-free.
- **Bootstrap friction.** First run downloads ~150MB Chromium; a slow/failed download looks like a broken feature.
- **Replay brittleness.** DOM changes break index-based flows — why replay is v2 (needs resilient selectors).

## Open Questions
1. **The ONE week-one task** — still unnamed. "Japanese account" is a *type*, not a start-to-finish task. Pins v1 acceptance.
2. **Driver model** — team's model, or **cloud-preferred** for browser sessions with local fallback? (Recommend cloud-preferred so v1 actually works.)
3. **Replay in v1 or v2?** Brief puts it **v2** so v1 proves the agentic-drive + persistent-login wedge first.
